_comment: Locked detection-regression baseline for Kavach's replay-based validation pipeline. Changing any value here is a REVIEWED act (Ishani + Parv) -- never automatic, never auto-retuned by a failing test. See VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md for the tiered runner (validate.py --tier A|B|C) that checks against this file.
_schema_note: Each entry's 'replayable' field is the authoritative machine-readable signal for whether validate.py can independently re-verify the number from the kavach-rearch working tree. replayable=false entries are historical reference values copied from another branch -- a passing Tier B/C run never re-checks them.

injecagent_ds_strict.note: 17 user cases x 32 DS attacker cases = 544. Provenance fires zero times on InjecAgent by design (no user_instruction/tool_output in InjecAgent's payload shape). Verified via concurrency=2 replay after the concurrency=8 run hit a Windows ProactorEventLoop connection-reset cascade -- see VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md's concurrency lesson.

agentdojo_provenance_applicable.value: 5/5 structurally-applicable attack cases ESCALATE via CHANNEL
agentdojo_provenance_applicable.note: 2/8 no-source-step + 1/8 no-destination-tool cases are structurally outside provenance's scope by design (NAVIGATOR's domain), not counted in this 5/5. Confirmed via the fixed harness (session_id uniqueness fix, tool_output threading fix, it.GOAL-vs-ut.PROMPT fix).

agentdojo_provenance_benign.note: KNOWN GAP: all 22 sessions are banking-suite only -- zero FP coverage exists yet for travel/workspace/slack benign behavior. Not a blocker, tracked as an open item. Separately (NOT part of this number): the full pipeline shows 3/22 hard BLOCK, decided_by NAVIGATOR+TRAJECTORY -- an unrelated, pre-existing interaction, tracked as its own distinct finding, never blended into CHANNEL's 5/22.

vault_executor_benign.note: Originally reported as 0/77; exhaustive cross-branch git history search (all 5 branches, full commit history, every JSON result file) found no trace of a 77-case dataset anywhere. 0/55 is the verified, replayable figure from parliament/benign_test_set/benign_v0.json (the only one of several superficially-similar 55-case files that actually carries real tool+args, not just a recorded verdict) -- confirmed 2026-07-18 by direct live replay against parliament/prefilters.py's current check_vault()/check_executor(), not reused from an old record.

navigator_tier_floor_malicious.note: REFERENCE ONLY. The mechanism this tests (parliament/navigator_tiers.py) does not exist on kavach-rearch -- navigator-rearch and kavach-rearch have genuinely diverged (navigator-rearch lacks tonight's CHANNEL provenance wiring; kavach-rearch lacks the tier-floor wiring). Cherry-picking the introducing commit (959ba43) was rejected because it also modifies parliament/server.py and would reintroduce NAVIGATOR-domain code onto kavach-rearch, crossing the branch-split boundary. Only the JSON data file was copied for registry lookup purposes. A passing Tier B/C run on kavach-rearch NEVER re-verifies this number -- see VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md.
navigator_tier_floor_malicious.source: commit 959ba43 on navigator-rearch, copied to kavach-rearch 2026-07-18

navigator_tier_floor_benign.note: REFERENCE ONLY, newly tracked as its own entry (same source file as navigator_tier_floor_malicious, distinct benign_results subset -- previously not separately tracked). 32 hand-constructed, obviously-legitimate calls, one per unique TIER_3 tool (InjecAgent's own user_cases.jsonl has no benign pairing for these tool names). All 32/32 ESCALATE is EXPECTED and ACCEPTABLE for this phase -- the tier floor has no context yet to distinguish a legitimate high-stakes call from a malicious one; this is a documented precision gap, not a false-positive regression. Not replayable from kavach-rearch -- see navigator_tier_floor_malicious's note.
navigator_tier_floor_benign.source: commit 959ba43 on navigator-rearch, copied to kavach-rearch 2026-07-18

navigator_channel_regression.note: REFERENCE ONLY. Confirms NAVIGATOR's tier floor firing redundantly alongside CHANNEL's read-then-send BLOCK on the same 29 cases doesn't interfere with CHANNEL's own detection (most-restrictive-wins in combine_verdicts() always picks BLOCK over ESCALATE). Not replayable from kavach-rearch -- see navigator_tier_floor_malicious's note.
navigator_channel_regression.source: commit 20f596d on navigator-rearch, copied to kavach-rearch 2026-07-18

latency_baseline.note: Isolated measurement only. The contended-environment replay timings from the 544-case concurrency=2 run (p50=4911.59ms, p95=9870.68ms) are EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED from this baseline -- they reflect concurrent load from other simultaneous work that night, not Kavach's own latency. Tier C latency checks compare against local reference measurements, not absolute numbers (CI hardware is not the Dell).
